source.title: Are Emergent Misaligned Models Self-Aware of their Misalignment? Latent Introspection in Activation Spaces of Niche Misaligned LLM

record.file_problem: None; the full paper is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study measures whether a base-model refusal representation transfers to an emergently misaligned model, using Procrustes alignment and projection scores rather than the claim's layer-wide direction ablation/addition.
record.gate_note: The study does not ablate or add the claimed single difference-in-means direction. Its causal patching, head ablations, and jailbreak results concern risk/refusal representations and specific suppression heads; they do not test the claimed direction intervention. Linear-probe and causal-patching results are recorded as findings about related representations, not as tests of the single-direction claim.
record.test_reason: The study builds a final-layer difference-in-means vector (risky minus benign financial prompts) in base Qwen2.5-32B and calls it a 'refusal vector'. It then uses that vector as a readout to analyse an emergently misaligned model, through Procrustes projection and patching effects on the projection. It never checks that this vector mediates refusal: no ablation or addition of it, and no refusal rate after intervening on it. The behavioural result, lower JailbreakBench ASR, comes from ablating two attention heads, not the direction. The base model is the pretrained Qwen2.5-32B, not a refusal-trained chat model. The positive projection of EM risky activations therefore shows that a risky-vs-benign axis is shared across the two models, not that a refusal-mediating direction transfers. That is a related construct, so the study does not test V1–V8.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that the EM Qwen2.5-32B model keeps and propagates its pre-fine-tuning safety/refusal representation, and that late-layer heads L62H12 and L62H28 suppress it. They frame emergent misalignment as suppression rather than erasure of safety training, and argue that ablating these heads restores safety.
record.recipe_differences: The study constructs a base-model refusal vector and aligns activation spaces with Procrustes analysis, then uses projection, component patching, and head ablation. It does not project out or add one direction at every layer and position, nor test preservation of general capabilities.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported causal effects vary by layer and component: Layers 24, 25, 32, 33, 62, and 63 are described as strong-positive patching locations, while Layers 15, 40, and 58 are near-zero or slightly adverse. The transfer analysis uses Procrustes alignment and a single risky-financial-advice prompt setting.

fits_no_version.finding: A risky-minus-benign mean-difference vector from base Qwen2.5-32B, rotated by benign-anchored Procrustes, separates EM-model risky from benign final-layer activations (mean 17.34 vs 0; d=5.30).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A risk/benign contrast axis computed in a pretrained base model is preserved, up to rotation, in an emergently misaligned fine-tune.

fits_no_version.finding: Risk-vs-benign is linearly decodable across layers in both base and EM models; randomized-label probes stay near chance.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Risk information is linearly decodable across many layers in both the base and EM models.

fits_no_version.finding: Patching risky MLP/attention activations into benign runs raises the final-layer projection at L24, 25, 32, 33, 62, 63, with near-zero effect at L15, 40, 58. Head-level patching finds positive effects for the L62 MLP, L62H15 and L62H31, and negative effects for L62H12 and L62H28.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Late-layer components in the EM model build up or suppress a projection onto the risk/'refusal' axis.

fits_no_version.finding: Ablating L62H12 cuts JailbreakBench ASR from 94.2% to 32.1% (mean) or 28.4% (zero); combined mean ablation with L62H28 brings it to about 5%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Two late-layer attention heads mediate safety suppression in this EM model; ablating them restores refusals.

record.peer_reviewed: Journal of Advances in Information Technology, Vol. 17, No. 5, 2026
record.problems: Only one 32B model and one risky-financial-advice niche are examined; the authors themselves call for cross-niche and cross-model replication. The study does not assess general capabilities. Many layerwise results are presented in plots rather than numerical text, and the reported transfer is representational rather than a causal test of user-facing refusal. The paper's description of the comparison model is not fully consistent: it refers to an original non-EM instruct model in one passage but identifies Qwen2.5-32B as the base model in the methodology.
record.rows_left_out: The detailed L62/L63 neuron- and head-level plots, SAE feature plots, and DLA plots are not separately extracted where the text does not provide a separable numerical outcome or explicit per-component result. The paper also mentions random-head-ablation results in the Fig. 11 caption without stating their values in the text.

untested.parts: No ablation or addition of a harmful-minus-harmless direction, no refusal rate after such intervention, no capability check.
Jailbreak ASR changes come from head ablation (L62H12, L62H28), not from suppression of or training against the direction.
No causal transfer test of a refusal-mediating direction from base to a fine-tuned variant. The base is pretrained Qwen2.5-32B, and only representational projection is reported.

record.verdict_notes: Other results not extracted bear on no version: DLA scores of −4.85 for L62H12 and −2.95 for L62H28; a logit-lens drop in 'sorry' probability at L62; random-head-ablation ASR (figure only); and SAE latent #2492. The paper is inconsistent on the comparison model: the introduction says the non-EM Instruct model, the methodology says pretrained Qwen2.5-32B. Only one model and one fine-tuning niche are used, and there is no capability check.

versions.untested_parts: Does not ablate or add one harmful-minus-harmless direction across layers and positions, measure user-facing refusal after that intervention, or assess general capabilities.
No weight edit or released-model abliteration is tested.
Does not test whether attacks suppress the claimed direction or whether training against its ablation adds robustness.
Does not compare affine, cone, or multiple-direction models of refusal geometry. Its circuit and head results do not directly establish the number or geometry of refusal directions.
Does not test a model's harmfulness judgment separately from its refusal decision.
Tests representational alignment for one base/EM model pair and one financial-advice prompt setting only; it does not test languages or multiple model variants.
Does not vary how or when refusal training is applied.

rows.subject: Qwen2.5_32BInstruct_risky_financial_advice
rows.operation_detail: Project EM-model activations onto the base model's refusal vector after Procrustes alignment.

conditions.value: Qwen2.5-32B refusal vector aligned by Procrustes analysis

rows.measure: Mean projection score onto the aligned refusal vector; distribution comparison also reported.
rows.note: Authors interpret the positive score and distribution difference as alignment between the EM model's risk representation and the base model's refusal representation. This is representational transfer, not a test of refusal behavior after intervening on the vector.
rows.check: The 'refusal vector' is a risky-minus-benign mean difference in the pretrained base model, never validated as refusal-mediating. A projection score is not a refusal measure, so this cannot show V6 transfer of a refusal direction. The Procrustes rotation is fitted only on benign activations, and risky/benign are linearly separable in both models (r3, r5). A positive projection is therefore close to expected by construction.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Base-model refusal vector transferred by Procrustes alignment to the risky-financial-advice EM model
reader_labels.reason: The EM model's risky-prompt projection was positive (17.34) while the benign set defined the zero point, supporting representational transfer in this tested model pair (r1, r2).
